json.name: Galaxy Formation and Evolution Simulation Workflow
json.description: A comprehensive computational workflow for simulating the formation and co-evolution of dark matter halos and baryonic structures, such as stars and gas, into galaxies within a cosmological context. It includes modules for initial condition generation, N-body dynamics, smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH), stellar feedback, black hole accretion, and post-processing analysis.

softwareRequirements.name: MPI (Message Passing Interface)
softwareRequirements.description: For parallel execution across multiple nodes.

softwareRequirements.name: OpenMP
softwareRequirements.description: For shared-memory parallelism within a node.

softwareRequirements.name: HDF5
softwareRequirements.description: For efficient storage and retrieval of simulation data.

softwareRequirements.name: NumPy & SciPy
softwareRequirements.description: Python libraries for numerical operations and scientific computing.

softwareRequirements.name: High-Performance Computing (HPC) Cluster
softwareRequirements.description: Requires significant computational resources (CPU cores, RAM, storage) typically found in supercomputing centers.

about.name: Galaxy Formation
about.description: The astrophysical process by which galaxies form and evolve over cosmic timescales.

input.name: Initial Cosmological Conditions
input.description: Input files specifying the initial distribution of dark matter and baryonic particles, including cosmological parameters (e.g., Omega_m, Omega_b, H_0, sigma_8). Typically generated by a separate perturbation code.

output.name: Simulated Galaxy Catalogs and Snapshots
output.description: Output data including particle snapshots at various cosmic times, properties of identified galaxies and halos (e.g., mass, stellar mass, star formation rates, merger trees), and derived observable quantities.
